summary: Online research sweep (projects/costs, parameter verification, SP data access, market/regulation) with adversarial claim verification

key_findings: Every WebFetch was blocked by the egress proxy, so all values are flagged S (search snippet or secondary news) or D (derived). No V values were obtained.

13 new projects found (ids 21-33). Orizon dominates the landfill pipeline: Jaboatão-PE R$258M for ~108k m3/d (inaugurated Mar 2026); Tremembé-SP 32.4k Nm3/d for ~R$109.2M (REIDI); Fazenda Rio Grande-PR R$241.76M (REIDI), sharing 170k m3/d with Guatapará-SP; Itapevi-SP 25k m3/d Edge offtake; Piratininga ~25k m3/d; three NE plants at ~R$150M each; RJ JV with Gás Verde at 2x100k m3/d.

Agro and manure segment, absent from the registry: H2A + Copercampos, Campos Novos-SC (swine manure), 16k m3/d for R$65M including a CO2 unit; Agric (Energisa), Campos Novos-SC, 25k m3/d for R$80M; Lurean Tulipa, Carambeí-PR, 31,440 Nm3/d for R$116.05M (REIDI Portaria 231/2026). Derived specific CAPEX is R$3,200-4,100 per m3/d.
Copersucar: up to R$600M for two new mill plants (50-60k m3/d, per plant vs combined unclear), construction late 2026/early 2027, inside an R$8 bi 10-year plan.

Corrections to existing rows. Atvos capacity is ~28 Mm3 per harvest, not per year. Adecoagro's 30k Nm3/d is NEW capacity (D: diesel replaced 8M L vs 2M L today implies roughly 5x total). São Martinho has been operating since Oct 2025 at ~15.6 Mm3 per harvest (248 d at 63k, consistent with harvest-day basis), co-financed by BNDES + FINEP. Raízen Costa Pinto is 72k Nm3/d plus 160 t/d CO2, consistent with 26 Mm3/yr on an annual-average basis.

BNDES funding splits: BP Edéia Fundo Clima R$193.4M + Finem R$51.4M; Bioo Fundo Clima R$101.5M + Finem R$47.1M; GNR Mauá/Vila Velha Fundo Clima + Finem. Gás Verde's R$131.1M (May 2025) covers Igarassu biomethane (R$90.2M) and the Seropédica bio-CO2 liquefaction unit (R$51.3M).
Landfill specific CAPEX benchmark R$2,300 per m3/d is supported by Jaboatão (2,389) and Mauá + Vila Velha (2,526). The small landfill at Tremembé (3,370) points to a scale effect.

Grid connection evidence: ES Gás will invest R$7M to connect the Vila Velha plant (headline only). The Caieiras-Comgás link needs ~5.3 km of network plus a Bio-Citygate (no cost found). TUSD-Verde is to be expressed in R$/m3 and cover interconnection O&M and investment only; no value is published. Comgás expects 800k m3/d of biomethane injection from new connections.
The LCOB R$0.78-1.83/m3 (sugar-energy, 2 Mt/yr), registered as EPE in parameters.csv, is attributed in a 2026 snippet to Instituto 17 (2022) RT08. It should be re-attributed.

EPE snippet: 4 sugar-energy projects (3 SP + 1 MT) total ~230k Nm3/d for R$838M CAPEX, which derives to R$3,643 per Nm3/d. A separate EPE figure of ~R$35 bi to meet biomethane supply 2026-2035 conflicts in scope with the R$3.0 bi for 25 units in R02.
The MME REIDI portarias are the best primary source for paired capacity and CAPEX data (company, CNPJ, Nm3/d, R$). They were blocked here and are the top item to verify.

key_findings: No row could be promoted to V. Egress policy blocked every primary/open-access host (mdpi, IPCC NGGIP, PMC, EuropePMC, EPE, legisweb, bioRxiv, SciELO, CORE, Semantic Scholar, DTU Orbit, OSTI, SGC, UNICAMP/USP/UNESP repositories). Only GitHub, GitLab and PyPI were reachable. All new evidence is S, from search snippets or secondary sources.

ANP Res. 1.006/2026 (S): PCS (HHV) is 35,000-43,000 kJ/m3 for CO/SE/S and 34,000-38,400 for the North. Wobbe is 46,500-53,500 kJ/m3 (40,500-45,000 North). Both are referred to 20 C, 101.325 kPa, dry basis. Converted to the project's 0 C basis, the PCS floor is 37.6 MJ/Nm3, which implies at least ~94% CH4 unless the gas is enriched with hydrocarbons (allowed only for PCS/Wobbe adjustment).
Proposed hhv_biomethane = 38.4 MJ/Nm3 (0 C) [37.6-39.8], flag D. It is derived from a K constant (pure CH4 HHV 39.82 MJ/Nm3) and an assumed 96.5% CH4, so it needs an ISO 6976 check.

bmp_fullscale is mis-attributed. Janke 2020 (Renew. Energy) gives continuous CSTR 224 mL CH4/g VS against batch BMP 185/174/222, so continuous is at or above batch (ratio about 1.0-1.3), not 0.85. Flag K and find another source.
fc_bmp conflict: Janke 2015 IJMS batch gives 245-281 NmL/g VS, above the registry high of 260.

b0_cattle conflict: IPCC 2006 Latin America values (via secondary) are dairy 0.13 and other cattle 0.10 m3 CH4/kg VS, swine 0.29. The registry central of 0.20 is not an IPCC Latin America value. 2019 Refinement snippets give 0.24 for high-productivity dairy and 0.13 for low-productivity.
vin_k2o conflict: by mash type, K2O is 1.2-2.1 (juice), 3.34-4.6 (mixed) and 3.74-7.83 g/L (molasses). The registry high of 4.6 excludes molasses vinasse.
Vinasse leaves distillation at about 90 C (Volpi preprint) or 85-90 C (PT secondary sources). This supports the 55 C thermophilic choice. Proposed as new param vin_temp. Vinasse density: not found.

Janke 2015 vinasse BMP: 246/273/302 NmL CH4 per g COD added. Barbosa 2022 gives 0.40 L/g COD removed, above the 0.35 theoretical at 0 C, so it is likely on a non-STP volume basis. The bases need harmonising.

Barbosa 2022 (JWPE 47) gives 30-day restart to 19 kg COD/m3/d, but in a UASB, not a CSTR. The registry high of 60 d has no source. The cod_so4_crit central of 10 interpolates between the two tested ratios (12 and 7.5), so it should be flagged D.

EPE OPEX factor R$0.150/Nm3 reconfirmed (S). The O&M basis is BNDES data for a reference plant of 33 Mm3/yr biogas giving 18.2 Mm3/yr biomethane (about 49.9k Nm3/d). The source document for the lcob_epe_sucro LCOB (0.78-1.83 R$/m3) is still unidentified.
CNPEM SUCRE assumes 140 kg straw DM/t cane, 50% recovery (scenarios 30/50/70%), 80 t cane/ha and a 35 km average straw radius, compared with the registry haul_dist of 25 km.

Hoffstadt 2020: up to 27% biogas loss after 6 months of ensiling (batch) and ~20% (Baserga) after 6 months. Volpi s-CSTR: 230 NmL CH4/g VS and 83 +/- 13% removal. Kiyuna 2017: -35% CH4 when COD/SO4 drops from 12 to 7.5. All re-confirmed at S.
New high-value lead: the Embrapa BiogasFert methodology PDF on biogas/biomethane potential from Brazilian swine and cattle herds.

gaps: No primary document was opened because of the egress allowlist, so no parameter could be promoted to V. Every row needs a V pass from an unrestricted network (queue in section 5 of the note).

ANP Res. 1.006/2026 limits for CH4, CO2, O2, N2, H2S, total S, dew point and methane number were not retrieved. Only PCS and Wobbe were seen in snippets, and the regional grouping conflicts between snippets (North vs North+Northeast).
IPCC 2006 Tables 10A-4 to 10A-9 and IPCC 2019 Table 10.16/10.16a B0 values are secondary/snippet-level only. Poultry B0 was not found.
The source document for lcob_epe_sucro (0.78-1.83 R$/m3) is still unidentified.
capex_epe value, price year and OPEX scope (feedstock, digestate, energy) were not re-seen. The EPE total OPEX conflicts: R$5.0 bi in the snippet vs R$1.1 bi in R02.
Vinasse COD and sulfate values from Fuess et al. 2018 STOTEN (doi:10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.03.326) were not retrieved. Vinasse density was not found anywhere.
olr_max_cstr and hrt_cstr have no new evidence. The Janke 2015 IJMS 16:23210 open PDF is located but blocked.
straw_bmp was not re-searched (search budget).
upg_ch4_recovery (membrane) was not found. The SGC 270 (Bauer 2013) OSTI copy is blocked.
The source of the 0.85 BMP-to-full-scale factor is unknown, and its cited source (Janke 2020) contradicts it.
The 4-month filter cake/energy cane storage loss values (6-16% / 13-22%) were not re-seen.
The pure-CH4 HHV constant (39.82 MJ/Nm3) and the IPCC 0.67 kg/m3 volume basis are prior knowledge and need ISO 6976 / IPCC Eq. 10.23 verification.
